title: Bank Deposit Recall Fee Reductions for Prompt Requests
content:
A Bank Deposit recall requested soon after the money was deposited takes a prompt-request reduction off the recall fee. Promptness is counted in calendar days from the transfer's deposit date to the handling date of the request.

## The rule

A recall requested no more than 3 calendar days after the deposit date takes the prompt-request reduction of 4.00 US dollars; one requested after that but no more than 10 calendar days after the deposit date takes the follow-up reduction of 2.00 US dollars; any later request takes no reduction.

The reduction is subtracted, in dollars, from the recall fee that would otherwise be charged on the request: it is not itself scaled by any percentage, the recall fee never goes below zero, and rounding to the cent happens once, on the final fee.

## Days after deposit and reduction

| Calendar days from the deposit date to the request | Reduction |
|---|---|
| 0 to 3 | 4.00 |
| 4 to 10 | 2.00 |
| 11 or more | none |

## Questions the rule answers

**The recall is requested on the third day after the deposit date. Which reduction?** 4.00; three days is no more than the prompt-request window.

**The recall is requested on the fourth day.** 2.00; it is after the prompt-request window but within 10 days.

**The recall is requested on the tenth day.** 2.00; ten days is no more than the follow-up window.

**The recall is requested on the eleventh day.** No reduction.

**Can the reduction take the fee below zero?** No. If the fee otherwise charged were 3.00 (a hypothetical figure), a 4.00 reduction would leave a fee of 0.00, not a negative amount.
